title: Routing Wizard: preflight validation + simulated traffic preview in Console
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary:
Enable a guided 'Routing Wizard' in Console that runs preflight checks and a simulated traffic preview when customers create or edit smart routing policies (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants). The goal is to reduce misconfigurations, surface cost/latency trade-offs up-front, and let customers preview how traffic will be routed before saving changes.

Problem / Motivation:
- Customers frequently configure routing policies that are valid syntactically but fail in production due to region outages, capacity tier mismatches, or incompatible model variants (e.g., quantized variant not allowed for function-calling).
- Current Console editor offers basic validation but lacks a deterministic preflight run or a cost/latency preview, leading to support tickets and rollout rollbacks.

Proposal (high level):
1) Add a preflight validation step that checks: region availability for the account (quotas & permitted regions), tier eligibility (Dedicated/Hosted/Private constraints), model compatibility matrix (function-calling, streaming, quantization), and any policy conflicts with organization-level restrictions.
2) Provide a simulated traffic preview (sample request profile or percent split) producing a per-route estimate: expected median latency, estimated token cost, and fallback hit probability. Use recent telemetry snapshots for realistic numbers.
3) Surface actionable warnings and suggested remediations (e.g., "Model X in ap-southeast-1 has no Dedicated capacity — consider fallback to model X-small or switch region to us-west-2").
4) Allow users to run additional 'what-if' scenarios: change region/tier/variant and re-run simulation inline.
5) Integrate links to related artifacts: rollout plans, canary settings, and a one-click create-canary option for high-risk changes.

Design constraints & trade-offs considered:
- Telemetry privacy: simulated preview should use aggregate, anonymized telemetry; do not surface customer-specific usage from other accounts.
- Cost of simulation: keep preview computation lightweight (cache last 6 hours of route metrics) and fall back to heuristic estimates when telemetry is cold.
- UX complexity: progressive disclosure — show a compact summary by default, expand to detailed per-route breakdown on demand.

Acceptance criteria:
- UI: Routing Wizard is available for new/edit policy flows and has a 'Run Preflight & Preview' CTA before Save.
- Validation: At least five validation checks implemented (region quota, tier mismatch, model incompatibility, routing loop detection, org-policy block).
- Simulation: Preview returns median latency and estimated token cost for sample traffic profile (low/medium/high) within 15s for cached telemetry, and within 60s for cold estimates.
- Remediation suggestions present for each warning, linking to Console docs and recommended config changes.
- Tests: End-to-end tests for happy path, a sample failure path (region denial), and fallback variant simulation.
- Metrics: Track "preflight_runs" and "preflight_warnings_shown" and % of runs that lead to abort (do not save).

Implementation notes / pointers:
- Backend: reuse the routing evaluation service used by runtime for policy decisions (ENG-2389) but add a preview mode that returns metric estimates rather than making routing decisions.
- Telemetry: use aggregated per-region/model latency/cost snapshots stored in observability (console-telemetry) with TTL=6h. If no snapshot available, run a fast heuristic estimator based on model family and sequence length percentiles.
- UX: compact summary card + expandable per-route table with color-coded warnings. See design frames: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Routing-Wizard-Preflight?node-id=42%3A7
- Docs & runbook: Confluence spec + rollout checklist: https://confluence.redwood-inference.internal/display/ENG/Routing+Wizard+Preflight
- GitHub link for prototype backend: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1234

Rollout plan:
- Beta: opt-in for 10% of orgs and selected customers who requested safer rollouts. Monitor save-abort rate and support tickets for 2 weeks.
- Full roll-out: after beta metrics satisfactory, enable by default but allow org-level disable flag.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Which telemetry retention window balances accuracy vs cost? (Proposed: 6 hours cached snapshots + heuristics)
- Should simulation include cost of any fallback model licensing (enterprise-only models)? (security/legal needs to confirm)
- Performance SLO for preflight should be < 15s for cached runs. If we cannot meet this, we need async preview with notification.

Related tickets & artifacts:
- Parent initiative: PM-5032 (routing policy builder enhancements)
- Backend dependency: ENG-2389 (routing evaluation service preview endpoint)
- Design task: DES-412 (routing-wizard mocks)
comments: 2026-01-12 — Aisha Kumar: Initial triage done with ENG and Design. Design suggested progressive disclosure for the preview details (summary + expand). Added DES-412 as dependency.

2026-01-25 — Priya Singh (Design reviewer): Requested clearer CTAs for 'Run preflight' vs 'Save anyway' and an inline help tooltip explaining how cost is estimated. Shared Figma frames and asked for copy review.

2026-01-27 — Security (Nadia Ortega): flagged potential issue with using cross-account telemetry. Confirmed preview must only use aggregated anonymous metrics. Marked ticket for security review (security_review_required=true).

2026-01-30 — Marco Liu: Prototype backend PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1234. Backend returns per-route estimated latency/cost and reason codes for warnings. Needs integration test and API schema doc.
2026-02-02 — Aisha Kumar: Updated acceptance criteria to include tracking metrics (preflight_runs, preflight_warnings_shown). Added rollout plan with 10% beta.
2026-02-10 — QA (TBD): Add e2e tests for the wizard. Tests to include simulated telemetry cold path and a case where org policy blocks a region.
